dishes.text: Delicious smash burgers with an optional egg

recipe.title: Double Smash Burgers with Onion Crust, Burger Sauce and an Optional Fried Egg
recipe.description: Two lacy-edged, deeply browned beef patties per bun with melted American cheese, sweet griddled onion, cold crisp lettuce and tomato, tangy burger sauce and a buttered toasted brioche bun — with a runny-yolked fried egg on top if you want one.

ingredients.item: Green leaf lettuce, leaves separated, washed and dried (new buy)
Onions, white, peeled and sliced paper-thin
Tomatoes, raw, cored and cut into 6 mm slices

steps.title: Portion the raw beef
steps.content: Divide the cold raw ground chuck into 12 loose balls of about 80 g each. Roll them just enough to hold together — do not compact them, and do not season them yet; salt on raw beef ahead of time tightens the texture and kills the crust. Set the balls on a plate and return them to the refrigerator until you're ready to cook.

steps.title: Mix the burger sauce
steps.content: In a bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, ketchup, yellow mustard, sweet relish, paprika, onion powder and garlic salt until smooth and pale orange. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper. Cover and refrigerate — it gets better after 20 minutes.

steps.title: Set up the garnish tray
steps.content: Lay out the paper-thin sliced onion, the sliced tomato (season the slices with salt and pepper to taste), the drained pickle chips and the lettuce leaves on a tray. Have everything within arm's reach of the stove — smash burgers cook in under 4 minutes and you will not have time to chop later.

steps.title: Butter and toast the buns
steps.content: Split the buns and spread the softened butter over all 12 cut faces. Heat a large skillet on the stove over medium (5 of 10) and toast the buns cut-side down in batches, 60–90 seconds, until deep golden. Stack them on a plate and wipe the skillet clean.

steps.title: Get the pan ripping hot
steps.content: Set a heavy cast-iron or carbon-steel skillet (or two, to move faster) on the stove over high heat (9–10 of 10) for 5 full minutes. Add 1 tbsp avocado oil and swirl — it should shimmer and just barely smoke. Turn on your hood or crack a window; this is a smoky cook and that smoke is the flavor.

steps.title: Smash the first batch
steps.content: Place 3 or 4 raw beef balls in the dry-hot pan, spaced well apart — do not crowd or they'll steam instead of crust. Immediately smash each one flat with a stiff spatula or a burger press backed by a second spatula, pressing hard for about 10 seconds until roughly 12 cm wide and thin enough to see the lacy edges. Season the tops with salt and pepper to taste, then press a small pile of the thin-sliced onion into each patty. Cook undisturbed 90–120 seconds, until the edges are dark brown and crisp.

steps.title: Flip, cheese, and pull
steps.content: Scrape under each patty with the spatula edge so the whole browned crust lifts with it, and flip onion-side down. Lay a slice of American cheese on each and cook 45–60 seconds more, until the cheese is slumping and the onion is caramelized. Stack the patties in cheesed pairs on a warm plate and tent loosely with foil.

steps.title: Repeat for the remaining batches
steps.content: Scrape the pan clean between rounds, add a touch more avocado oil if it looks dry, let it come back to full heat for 30–45 seconds, and repeat the smash-season-onion-flip-cheese sequence until all 12 patties are done. Six stacks of two, cheese between and on top.

steps.title: Fry the optional eggs
steps.content: Wipe the skillet, lower the heat to medium-low (4 of 10) and add the remaining 1 tbsp avocado oil. Crack in the eggs, season with salt and pepper to taste, and fry 2–3 minutes until the whites are fully set and the edges are crisp but the yolks are still runny. Cook in two batches if your pan is crowded.

steps.title: Build and serve
steps.content: Spread burger sauce generously on both toasted bun faces. Bottom bun, lettuce, tomato slices, pickle chips, then the double cheesed patty stack, then a fried egg if you're using one, then the top bun. Press gently, serve immediately while the cheese is still molten — smash burgers wait for nobody.

recipe.notes: Protein per serving: about 56 g (with the egg). Calories per serving: about 1180 (with the egg). New buys: ground beef chuck 80/20, brioche buns, American cheese, butter, mayonnaise, yellow mustard, green leaf lettuce, dill pickle chips — everything else comes from your pantry. Make-ahead: the burger sauce holds 5 days covered in the fridge and improves overnight; slice the onion, tomato and portion the beef balls up to 4 hours ahead and keep covered in the refrigerator. Pro tips: the beef must go into the pan COLD and unseasoned for the best crust; smash within the first 10 seconds of contact or the patty won't spread; use a firm metal spatula and scrape, never lift, so the crust comes with the meat; never press a patty after the flip or you'll squeeze out the fat that makes it taste like a smash burger. Leftover patties reheat well in the Tovala on Reheat for 4 minutes, then 1 minute on Broil to re-crisp the edges.

dishes.text: Either you can think of something, or nothing

recipe.title: Either You Can Think of Something, or Nothing
recipe.description: Craggy smashed baby potatoes roasted until the edges shatter like chips, drenched in garlic butter, blistered under parmesan, and finished with lemon and parsley so every piece tastes like the crispy corner of the pan.

ingredients.item: Baby potatoes (The Little Potato Co.), scrubbed, left whole
Salt (for the boiling water and for seasoning)

ingredients.amount: 45 g, plus a little extra for the pan

ingredients.item: Parsley, fresh, leaves finely chopped, stems discarded (new buy)
Lemon, raw — zested, then halved for juice (new buy)

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.content: Put the scrubbed whole baby potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water by 5 cm, and salt the water heavily (it should taste like a good soup). Bring to a boil over high heat (9–10), then drop to a simmer (3–4) and cook 18–20 minutes, until a paring knife slides into the biggest potato with zero resistance. Underboiled potatoes will not smash — they crumble or bounce, so err on the tender side.

steps.title: Drain and steam-dry
steps.content: Drain the potatoes in a colander and let them sit, uncovered, for 5 minutes. The surface moisture flashes off and that dry skin is what turns crisp later. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 230°C / 450°F and lightly oil a large sheet pan with olive oil.

steps.title: Make the garlic butter
steps.content: In a small saucepan over low heat (2–3), melt the 115 g butter with the 45 g olive oil and the 2 tablespoons minced garlic. Warm gently 2–3 minutes, swirling, just until the garlic smells sweet and the butter is fully liquid — do not let the garlic take on color or it will turn bitter in the oven. Stir in the 1 teaspoon dried oregano and pull off the heat.

steps.title: Smash
steps.content: Arrange the warm potatoes on the oiled sheet pan with space between each one. Press each potato flat with the bottom of a heavy glass or a measuring cup until it's about 1.5 cm thick and the edges split and fray — those ragged edges are the crispy part, so don't chase neat discs. Work in a single layer; use two pans if they crowd.

steps.title: Butter and season
steps.content: Spoon or brush about half the garlic butter over the smashed potatoes, getting it into the cracks. Season generously with salt and pepper on top.

steps.title: Roast
steps.content: Roast on the oven's upper-middle rack at 230°C / 450°F for 25 minutes, until the undersides are deep gold and the edges are visibly crisp. Rotate the pan front-to-back once at the halfway mark for even color. Don't flip them — the flat bottom is doing the work.

steps.title: Butter again, then parmesan
steps.content: Pull the pan out. Spoon the remaining garlic butter over the potatoes, scraping in all the garlic solids from the pan, then scatter the 60 g grated parmesan evenly over the top.

steps.title: Broil to finish
steps.content: Switch the oven to broil and return the pan to the top rack for 3–4 minutes, until the parmesan is melted and browned in patches. Stand at the oven and watch it — at this distance it goes from golden to burnt in under a minute.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.content: Slide the potatoes onto a warm platter. Zest the lemon over the top, then squeeze about half the lemon's juice over everything. Shower with the chopped parsley, add a final pinch of salt and a few grinds of pepper, and serve immediately while the edges are still shattering-crisp.

recipe.notes: Protein per serving: about 8 g. Calories per serving: about 405. New buys: unsalted butter, freshly grated parmesan, fresh parsley, 1 lemon. Make-ahead: boil and smash the potatoes up to 6 hours ahead, leave them buttered on the sheet pan at room temperature, then roast right before guests sit down — the second half of the butter, the parmesan and the broil all happen à la minute. Pro tips: salt the boiling water aggressively, since it's the only chance to season the inside of the potato; give each potato breathing room on the pan, because a crowded pan steams instead of crisping; and add the lemon juice only at the table — do it early and the crust softens. Leftovers keep 3 days covered in the fridge and come back to life in the air fryer at 200°C / 400°F for 5–6 minutes in a single layer.
